summary: sitecard broadcasts live public SSH endpoint URLs to a hardcoded ntfy.sh topic by default
details: sitecard exposes a workspace directory over SSH via public relays (srv.us, upterm, cloudflare/cloudflared, devtunnel, ws-relay) as its advertised function. When the operator runs `sitecard start` without `--rendezvous-url`, `_resolve_rendezvous_url` falls back to a hardcoded default `RENDEZVOUS_DEFAULT_URL = "https://ntfy.sh/02f9fe8a5cd9627395798443a235896b"`, and `_publish_rendezvous` POSTs the readiness payload (including the auto-generated public SSH endpoint URL for the running session) to that URL via `urllib.request.urlopen`. ntfy.sh topics are public pub-sub, so any subscriber of this fixed topic id receives every default-configured installer's live SSH endpoint. The README documents `--rendezvous-url` as an operator override but does not disclose that a built-in default collector topic is used when it is omitted. Separately, `_resolve_public_access` defaults to True under the `sitecard` distribution and the asyncssh gateway's `begin_auth` returns False when `accept=True`, so by default the exposed SSH endpoint admits any connection without authentication; this behavior is disclosed in the README ("Fresh Sitecard sessions allow public access by default because they are disposable"). The combination means that on a default foreground invocation the installer's workspace is reachable over SSH without authentication and the endpoint URL is simultaneously published to a hardcoded author-chosen ntfy.sh topic. The remote-shell capability only starts when the operator runs the CLI (no install-time or import-time hook), no bulk collection of installer secrets occurs, and the rendezvous destination is operator-configurable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
